facts.claim: run.sh looks for uv on PATH first. If that fails it falls back to $HOME/.local/bin/uv, because hooks run under a non-login shell.
With no uv, a session hook prints an 'install uv' warning at most once every 24h (tracked by a marker file) and exits 0. `--warm` instead exits 1.
To check whether the environment is ready, run.sh asks uv to import multiplai_core with `--frozen --no-sync`. It does not guess the venv path.

`--warm` runs `uv sync` synchronously and exits with uv's status. On success it clears the `.warmup` marker no matter who owns it. On failure it records the exit code, but only if this run owns the marker.
Warm path: if the environment is ready, run.sh execs the hook script under `uv run` before it looks at any marker.

Cold start: whichever hook wins an atomic `mkdir .warmup` spawns a detached `sh -c` builder. The builder writes its own pid, runs `uv sync` into .warmup.log, and on failure leaves a `status` file holding the exit code.

Marker triage: a `status` file means the build failed, and the marker is reaped after 15 minutes. A dead pid means the builder died, also reaped after 15 minutes. Any marker older than 60 minutes is reaped regardless.
While the build is running or has failed, only context_manager.py and session_start.py print the notice to stdout. Every hook prints it to stderr, then exits 0.

session_end, pre_compact, session_stop and session_notification save their stdin payload. A detached subshell polls every 2s, up to 300 times, then replays the hook. If the environment never comes up it logs a 'dropped' line to .warmup-deferred.log.
Once .warmup-deferred.log passes 256 KiB it is rotated by an atomic `mv` to `.1`, so only one old copy is kept.

GeneratorBase is a template method. run() loads state and the existing catalog, discovers sources, generates entries for changed sources, prunes deleted ones, checks for lost hand fields, and writes the catalog plus state unless this is a dry run or the client is a stub.
A source is skipped only if its sha256 matches the stored hash AND an entry for it already exists, and only when force is off.
Entries are generated concurrently, bounded by an asyncio.Semaphore of config.catalog_concurrency.

_call_llm retries only on status codes 429/500/502/503. It makes up to 3 retries with backoff of 0.1*2^attempt seconds; any other error is raised at once.

orchestrator.run_orchestrator is the main entry point. It re-binds to an existing worktree, finds or creates the BuildState, then runs the phases in order, each guarded by state.is_phase_complete: BOOTSTRAP, INTERVIEW, RESEARCH, CODEBASE_ANALYSIS (+spec-extract), EPIC_SPLIT, SPEC_GENERATION, DESIGN_AUDIT, PLAN_REVIEW, the size gate, PROTOTYPE, REVIEW, TDD_BUILD, DOCS_UPDATE, RESPEC, archive, PUBLISH.

The orchestrator talks to the SKILL.md wrapper through stdout markers such as PHASE:<X>:COMPLETE, WORKTREE:, BRANCH:, PR:, RESULT:SUCCESS and BUILD:COMPLETE:. It also records each transition on the board through board.record.

Error handling in run_orchestrator works like this. SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt and CancelledError are recorded as an interruption (the checkpoint is re-saved, the state is not marked FAILED) and re-raised. Any other exception logs, posts a board failure if the build had not yet succeeded, and returns 1. A BUDGET summary is always written in the finally block.

A failed run that leaves a dirty registry also returns 1.

facts.claim: tdd_engine.py is the block-by-block test-first build engine. It parses tasks.md into blocks, runs TDD cycles for each block, gates each block on integration tests and quality reviews, and exits with 0 (success), 1 (build failure) or 4 (agent timeout).

parse_blocks splits tasks.md on `## N. Name` headers. It reads a `Satisfies:` line, an `Interfaces:` section with `- Produces:`/`- Consumes:` bullets, and either checkbox tasks (standard format) or a free description (advanced format). A missing file returns [] with a warning.

run_tdd_engine configures the budget, loads or creates BuildState, builds TDDState from tasks.md, runs a baseline test gate once, then loops over the blocks. For each block it runs run_block_tdd and then _run_integration_and_review, followed by a whole-change refactor, mutation testing and an optional entry-point check.

run_block_tdd stamps a pre-block baseline commit (the empty-tree SHA in a repo with no commits). It then runs the test writer, the static and LLM test-quality gate, and the RED gate, then the implementer, then an optional refactorer. Each phase is committed as `<phase>(block-N): name`.

facts.claim: The static weak-test scan fails a block when 20% or more of its test functions match weak patterns, or when it finds no `def test_` at all. A failing scan goes to an LLM auditor; if the auditor confirms it, the test writer gets one retry, and weak tests after that fail the block.

facts.claim: When the RED gate passes, the engine stores sha256 hashes of the block's test files. unchanged_tests_gate later compares against these in each writable window. A change that the agent declared (flagged) passes, but its claim is recorded and the baseline is reset to the new hashes.

If the integration gate fails, up to 3 integration-fix attempts run, and the last one is 'escalated' to a different model step. Then up to 3 review iterations run: each review is adjudicated, recorded, and scored, and an implementer fix follows a failing score unless it was the last iteration.

Fix on pass: when a block passes review, one extra fix pass runs on its accepted findings from a clean checkpoint commit. The fix is kept only if the tests stay green and the block still passes review; otherwise the tree is rolled back while keeping the review round records, and the findings are written to unfixed-findings.md.
